lawyer:
Aftabuddin, Advocate — For the Petitioner. 
Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with A Qushem Md. Fazlul Huq Khan, Advocates — For the Opposite Party. 
Dewan Zaman, Deputy Attorney-General — Amicus Curiae
parties:
Talukder Sarwar Hossain and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Dr. Shakhawat Hossain and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
ARM Amirul Islam Chowdhury J: This Rule was issued on the plaintiff opposite party and defendant opposite parties to show cause as to why petitioners Talukder Sarwar Hossain and Md. Abdur Rouf Mondal should not be allowed to file a memo of appeal in this Court under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and decree respectively dated 4.11.92 and 8.11.92 passed by Mr. Shahidul Haque, Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 for specific performance of a contract.

2. It is necessary to state the petitioners case as stated in his application on which the present Rule has been issued. It appears that the petitioners entered into a contract for purchase of the suit property with defendant No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed through his mother Mrs. Sarwatara Begum who was appointed by defendant No. 2 as his attorney by a deed of power of attorney dated 10.6.81 to protect, preserve and manage and sell the suit property. That the said Attorney Sarwatara Begum entered into a contract to sell the suit property with the petitioner on 6.12.85 on behalf of defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed for a consideration of Taka 25,00,000.00 on receipt of Taka 10,00,000.00 as earnest money on condition that she would execute and register the sale deed within 3 months from the date of bainapatra and put the petitioners into khas possession of one of the rooms of the suit property. That thereafter Sarwatara Begum the attorney of defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed claimed more money to procure necessary document and the petitioners paid to her a further sum of Taka 5,50,000.00 against a written receipt i.e. (by endorsement made on the back side of the bainapatra) and subsequently Sarwatara Begum the attorney died on 18.8.89 before she could execute and register the sale deed. After the death of Sarwatara the attorney, defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Ahmed admitted the bainapatra executed by his mother Sarwatara Begum the attorney on 1.9.89 on receipt of a further sum of Taka 1,50,000.00 by granting a written receipt. That defendant opposite party No. 2 used to remain almost always outside Dhaka so the petitioners could not complete the sale deed in respect of the suit property in spite of their best endeavors. That the petitioners managed to meet defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed in October, 1990 and approached him to execute and register the sale deed. Defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed told the petitioners that he required one lakh taka more for obtaining income tax clearance certificate and, as such, the petitioners paid him a further sum of Taka one lac on 12.10.90 against a written receipt and opposite party No. 2 undertook to execute and register the sale deed within six months on receipt of balance of the consideration money. That thereafter the defendant opposite party No. 2 failed to execute and register the sale deed and deferred the execution and registration of the sale deed on this plea or that plea and finally on 24.10.92 refused to execute and register the sale deed by saying that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain had filed a suit for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property against him, as such, it was not possible for him to execute and register the sale deed till the disposal of the concerned suit. The petitioners thereafter on getting information slip through his Advocate came to learn from the trial Court on 26.10.92 that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain had filed a suit being Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 for specific performance of contract against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed. That thereafter on 3.11.92 the petitioners filed Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 for specific performance of a contract in respect of the suit property and for cancellation of the bainapatra of plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed and opposite party No. 1 Shakhwat Hossain. On 4.11.92 the petitioners filed an application supported by an affidavit under sections 10 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for staying all further proceeding of Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 instituted by plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 Shakhawat Hossain against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed for specific performance of a contract in respect of the suit property till disposal of Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 or in the alternative for analogous hearing of both the suits. The learned Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Dhaka by his order dated 4.11.92 stayed all further proceedings of Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 till the disposal of Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 and on the same day i.e. on 4.11.92 decreed Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 in favour of plaintiff opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain.

3. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree respectively dated 4.11.92 and 8.11.92 passed in Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 the petitioners have presented a memo of appeal with appropriate court fee stamps before the stamp reporter of this Court who refused to entertain the memo of appeal on the grounds that the petitioners were not parties in Title Suit No. 34 of 1988. Hence the petitioners have filed this application for leave to appeal as third party under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

4. The plaintiff decree holder Dr. Shakhawat Hossain has filed counter affidavit. The petitioners have also filed an affidavit-in-reply. The plaintiff decree holder alleged that he entered into a contract for purchase of the suit property with defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed. In this connection the plaintiff decree holder filed Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Ahmed and obtained a decree in his favour by a judgment and decree respectively dated 4.11.92 and 8.11.92 in that suit. The plaintiff decree holder Dr. Shakhawat Hossain had already obtained a decree against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property. The petitioners had instituted on 3.11.92 Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 against defendant opposite party No. 2 for specific performance of contract in respect of the suit property. We have already stated that on 4.11.92 the petitioners who are the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 filed an application under section 10 read with section 151 CPC for staying all further proceedings of Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 till the disposal of Title Suit No. 241 of 1992. Under section 10 CPC the earlier suit cannot be stayed till the disposal of a latter suit. Section 10 CPC authorized the Court to stay all further proceedings of a latter suit till disposal of the earlier suit. In the circumstances the learned Subordinate Judge had correctly stayed all further proceedings of Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 till the disposal of Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 on 4.11.92 the petitioners could have at best filed an application for adding of them as defendants in Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 which the petitioners did not do. Whether such application for addition of parties under Order 1, rule 10 CPC could be allowed or not is entirely a different matter.

<u>5. The question before us is whether the petitioner as third party (who had not been parties in the suit) could be permitted to file an appeal in this court against the judgment and decree respectively dated 4.11.92 and 8.11.92 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 34 of 1988. The general principle of law is that a stranger had no right to be added as a party in a suit for specific performance of contract. Title suit No. 34 of 1988 was a suit for specific performance of a contract. In support of his contention Mr. Aftabuddin the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that third parties who had not been a party in the proceeding can also prefer an appeal against a decree or order if the concerned party is substantially affected by the decree or order. In this connection the learned Advocate Mr. Aftabuddin for the petitioners referred to the case of H M Saya & Co vs. Wazir Ali Industries Ltd. reported in 21 DLR (SC) 50. In respect of a stranger to be added as a party in a suit for specific performance of contract the learned Advocate for the petitioners has referred to the case of Bajranglal Agarwvala vs. Aksed Ali Shaikh and others reported in 35 DLR (HC) 110. The appeal in the case reported in 21 DLR (SC) arose out of an interlocutory order passed by the trial Court. The Supreme Court of Pakistan was of the view that the third party who preferred the appeal was deliberately not made a party in the suit by the plaintiff and that the order of injunction adversely affected only the third party appellant. In the circumstances held that under such circumstances an appeal by a third party is maintainable. In the case reported in 35 DLR 110 a Division Bench of this Court allowed a stranger third party to be added as a party in a suit for specific performance of a contract. In that case the co-sharer of the vendor in respect of the undivided suit property filed an application for adding him as a party in the suit instituted by the plaintiff for specific performance of a contract in respect of suit property which was not specially divided by metes and bounds among the co-sharers. In the instant case the position is quite different. Plaintiff Dr. Shakhawat Hossain alleged a contract for sale of the suit property against defendant-opposite party No. 2 in respect of the suit property and obtained a decree in his favour. Title suit No. 34 of 1988 by Dr. Shakhawat Hossain and Title Suit No.214 of 1992 by the petitioners are for specific performance of contract against the same vendor namely, defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed in respect of the same self property.</u>

<u>6. In Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 for argument's sake even if the petitioners had been made party the court would not be competent to pass a complete and effective remedy in favour of the petitioners. Title Suit No. 34 of 1988 could however be decreed or dismissed. Assuming for the time being that the suit of plaintiff Dr. Shakhawat Hossain (Title Suit No. 34 of 1988) is dismissed that could not give adequate and effective relief to the petitioners. For obtaining a decree for specific performance of contract against defendant-opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed the petitioner would have to institute a separate suit for specific performance of contract. As it appears the petitioners have already on 3.11.92 instituted Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 against defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed and plaintiff decree holder Dr. Shakhawat Hossain for specific performance of contract and other reliefs. In the circumstances whether we are in a position to grant leave to the petitioners (who had not been made parties in the suit) as their party to prefer an appeal in this Court against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 34 of 1988. The normal rule is only parties to the suit or proceeding is competent to prefer an appeal. In certain exceptional circumstances however a third party (who had not been a party in the suit or proceeding) may be permitted to prefer an appeal against the decree or order. The exceptional circumstances under which a third party may be allowed to prefer an appeal are where the subject matter of the appeal had been conclusively determined as to the rights of the parties including the third party with regard to any of the matters in controversy in the suit or proceedings and the party appearing must have been adversely affected by such determination i.e. the decision must operate as res judicata against the third party. As a general rule a decision cannot be said to adversely affect a third party unless it would operate as res judicata in any further suit or proceedings by or against the third party. In the instant case the third party has not been given the right to prefer an appeal by any statute in as much as the appeal is a creature of the statute. The suit being a suit for specific performance of a contract the petitioners being strangers having no right to be added as parties in the suit (being Title Suit No. 34 of 1988) had no right to prefer an appeal against the judgment and decree passed in the said suit. The subject matter of the appeal (concerned suit) had not been conclusively determined as to the rights of the parties including the third parties petitioners with regard to any of the matters in controversy in the suit. The third parties petitioners not being parties in the suit are not bound by the decree passed in the suit i.e. the decree passed in the concerned suit would not operate as res judicata against the third parties petitioners, as such; the third parties petitioners had not been adversely affected. It is stated by the third parties petitioners in their application that they had been put into possession in one of the rooms of suit property. If that is true then they may seek protection under section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act. In this connection reference may be made to the case of Mrs. June Ferguson vs Aminur Rashid Chowdhury reported in 25 DLR 1 and to the case of Mir Abul Ali vs. Md. Rafiqul Islam reported in 40 DLR (AD) 75. The third party petitioners had already instituted Title Suit No. 214 of 1992 against plaintiff decree holder opposite party No. 1 Dr. Shakhawat Hossain and defendant opposite party No. 2 Raisuddin Anwar Ahmed wherein the third parties petitioners may seek appropriate, adequate, complete and efficacious reliefs against them. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case we are not inclined to grant leave to the third parties petitioners to prefer an appeal against the judgment and decree passed in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 34 of 1988.</u>

7. For the reasons stated above the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.
